I see the `check_subs` block:

```c
uint8_t c = *fr_sbuff_current(&our_in);
```

This reads the current character from the input buffer. If the input buffer is exhausted (i.e., `our_in` points past the end), this would be an out-of-bounds read.

But wait - the `while (fr_sbuff_extend_lowat(&status, &our_in, needle_len) > 0)` loop checks if there's enough data. And `if (!fr_sbuff_diff(&our_in, &end)) break;` checks if we've reached the end.
